sentences.text: Good morning, Rob.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We still continue to see trending higher Prime Power.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Both turbines and reciprocating gensets.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: I've had a handful of discussions with customers for Prime Power just in this last quarter.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: So a lot of quoting activity continuing to go on.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And I think we'll continue to see that trend as we move into the future.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We're not seeing anything different in that space.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: When it comes to orders and sort of backlog, if it's significant order in gas Prime Power, we're probably looking at 2029.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: Would love to get just some sense of how you could see your mix shifting maybe that mix of prime versus backups

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: where you've been versus maybe where that mix is heading as you look to 2030.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Yeah, as we talk to our customers, we've not seen really any change since the last quarter in our discussions with customers.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We continue to see momentum in, you know, standby diesel backup, which has been the growing base of our business for quite a while, you know, before even really AI started to accelerate the growth even more, driven by a lot of demand for cloud compute.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Then, you know, AI has obviously accelerated that, you know, when it comes to prime power versus diesel, you know, that's one of the things that's, you know, good about the capacity we put in place.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: It's pretty fungible as long as we have line of sight to those orders.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: You know, if you get the largest 3520, you know, that one,

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: they're probably a little more extended on the gas 3520K.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: But keep in mind as well, the capacity we have in place and the momentum we have, you know, it's more than just power generation.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We continue to see the momentum there, oil and gas, and I think we're going to move a lot of natural gas in the next few years and a really strong in gas compression, both at solar turbines and in our reciprocating engine business.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Demand is there for that.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: It's for marine and large engines also go into our mining products as well.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: So as the mining picks up, you know, we're excited about, you know, making sure that we can serve those customers.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And really when you talk about, aside from diesel standby, all these other applications, we, as the field population grows, we need to be able to support customers

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: in the aftermarket and grow services.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: So the capacity is all aligned to what we plan to have.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: In place to meet our goals in 2030.

sentences.speaker: Operator
sentences.text: We'll go next to Kristen Owen at Oppenheimer.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: Hi, good morning.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: Thank you for the question.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: You know, we've talked a lot about the synchronous growth within the portfolio, but I'm hoping you can maybe double click for us on the construction side.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: You called out the tough comps here in the fourth quarter, but backlog growth in construction, can you maybe help us understand or give us some color on the underlying demand, how much of that growth is going into rental for your own fleet versus third parties, and maybe some of those other sources of demand outside of rental and mega projects.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Before we get into the quarter, I'd like to share my perspective on Danaher today and the opportunity ahead as I begin this next chapter as CEO.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: The opportunity for Danaher is straightforward, to become the defining leader in life sciences and diagnostics, a company that unambiguously gains share, delivers sustainable profitable growth, and helps our customers improve outcomes for patients around the world.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: The foundation we built at Danaher is strong.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We operate

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: leading businesses, foster deep customer relationships, and empower talented people, all enabled by the Danaher business system.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: At the same time, growth over the past several years has not consistently reflected the full potential of our portfolio.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We've navigated significant changes in our markets, but regardless of the environment, we hold ourselves to a higher standard.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We see a meaningful opportunity to accelerate sustainable core revenue, and to build a sustainable business model that is relationally anchored to ourcream efficient business model.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: It's great to see peopleAdditional capital, gains share, more consistently, and more fully translate the strengths of our portfolio into differentiated performance.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: I'm confident in what we built and I'm energized by what I've seen across Danaher these last few months.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Our focus now is strengthening execution and delivering on that potential.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Recently, I had a conversation with one of our executives preparing for a customer meeting related to Alzheimer's disease.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: It often has me wondered when I heard it so gracefully.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: I mean, it's a collision.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: First of all, what's a collision?

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: It' What started as a discussion about how one of our businesses could help address a particular part of that customer's challenge quickly expanded to cover the roles seven different operating companies could play across discovery, AI-enabled target selection, laboratory automation, process development, scale-up, and diagnostic testing.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And when the challenge is Alzheimer's disease, speed matters, both to the scientists working to understand it and the families waiting for answers.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: That conversation reinforced something important.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Our customers don't think about their challenges through the lens of our organizational structure.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: They have a problem to solve, and they want the best partnership and solutions we can bring them.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: I see this as critical to Danaher's next chapter.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: As some of our greatest opportunities sit at the intersections of our businesses.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We will preserve what makes our operating company structure advantage, the customer intimacy, the accountability, while making it easier to bring the full power of Danaher to our customers.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Our foundation and the power of the Danaher business system have given us leadership positions across the life sciences and diagnostic markets, and a unique role in helping accelerate the transition.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Our data and data science businesses have helped us transform our translation of scientific discovery into human impact.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Our life science businesses enable discovery, our biotechnology businesses help turn those discoveries into scaled and accessible therapies, and our diagnostics businesses help guide treatment.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Together, Danaher spans a broad path from experiment to patient, with DBS adding speed and operating discipline at scale.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We've already taken practical steps to show up as a more connected Danaher.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: In diagnostics, for example, we are successfully deepening customer relationships by bringing leaders from across our businesses together with key customers to look across the portfolio, better understand their priorities, and identify where a more coordinated approach can create additional value.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We do this by having our key diagnostics leaders in the same room at the same time with our key customers to understand their biggest pain points and where we can drive incremental value.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: This approach has generated meaningful incremental revenue opportunities

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: and is helping drive share gains across our diagnostics businesses.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And as we bring more of Danaher to our customers, we can also become more systematic about connecting capabilities across our businesses to solve more customer needs.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Algevron and Cytiva's recent collaboration deliver an end-to-end mRNA solution to the customer's customer experience.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: This solution is a great example, helping streamline our customers' development processes while meaningfully accelerating timelines.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Ultimately, our commercial strategy is straightforward.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Execute better and more entrepreneurially,

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: show up together as Danaher for our customers, and connect our capabilities where we can create greater value.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We will make it easier for customers to access the full strength of our customers, and create greater value.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We'll make it easier for customers to interact with us and know more about the experience of Danaher and look to us when trying to solve their most important challenges.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Our second priority is delivering more innovation.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Danaher is already at the forefront of innovation, but I believe strengthening our innovation capabilities represents one of our largest opportunities to accelerate long-term growth.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Delivering on our brand promise, innovation at the speed of life, means we will be deliberate and straightforward about our products and services.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: deliberate and strategic about where we invest in R&D and ensure we appropriately allocate resources behind our best ideas.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: That means more closely linking strategy and R&D investments, concentrating resources behind the highest potential initiatives, and working more closely across our businesses and external partners to move promising innovations.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We will also fund transformational opportunities at the enterprise level when we believe Danaher has a clear right to win and larger investment can create meaningful competitive advantage.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: These decisions will require clear choices and greater enterprise-level conviction about where we can create the most value.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Innovation cycles take time, but over the long term, we believe this more focused approach can support higher-end innovation.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Thank you.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And to me, this is the heart of innovation at the speed of life, helping promising science move faster towards the patients who need it.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Our third priority is being the home and destination for exceptional talent.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We believe our ability to attract and develop exceptional talent in science and technology AI, commercial and operating disciplines will increasingly set us apart from competitors.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We also need to develop and deploy our people more intentionally against Danaher's highest priority growth and innovation opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Danaher has given me that kind of exposure in my own career, learning DBS and then applying it across commercial, R&D, and business leadership.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: I want us to continue to create exceptional opportunity for the next generation of leaders.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: As we evolve DBS for the AI era, I believe we can create an even more compelling place for the best talent in our industry.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And our fourth priority is being more disciplined with our capital and resources.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: M&A and capital deployment have been essential drivers of Danaher's growth and will remain so.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We will maintain the robust investment criteria that has served us well for many decades while bringing strategic clarity and discipline to how we allocate capital and resources.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We are focused on deepening our positions in attractive markets and identifying strategically

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: compounding areas that build from the strengths we already have in our businesses.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Our objective is to deliver high returns on our investments with greater consistency, while positioning Danaher for sustainably differentiated and profitable growth.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Across each of these priorities, there is a common idea.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We create more value by building a stronger, more connected company.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: That doesn't mean changing what makes our operating companies successful.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: It means preserving their customer intimacy and accountability, while making it easier to share ideas, capabilities, talent, and resources.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: That's what Danaher does.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Danaher is a strong partner.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We need to socially contribute to more people's scaling.

sentences.text: I was particularly impressed by the process development team and how closely that team works side-by-side with customers to solve their most difficult challenges.

sentences.speaker: Management

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We're bringing innovation and process expertise to help customers solve those challenges, and importantly, we're seeing that differentiated approach help us win more specifications with customers.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Next, we recently announced our first AI-powered autonomous device.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: This is the first AI-powered autonomous device that we've launched in the Uppsala University's AI-powered autonomous device lab.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Based at Adcam, this lab brings together AI, robotics, and technologies from across our portfolio, including Cytiva, Beckman-Coulter Life Sciences, gene data, IDT, and molecular devices,

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: to offer a connected design, make, and test workflow.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: By continuously learning from each experiment, the platform is designed to help researchers move from the idea of a single reagent up to eight times faster, while generating up to 10 times higher volume compared to existing models, helping accelerate scientific discovery while providing the rigorous quality and reproducibility required to advance AI-driven drug discovery.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Our partnership with NVIDIA, announced last week, will further advance this vision by connecting our instruments and workflows with NVIDIA's capabilities to help shape autonomous science for our customers.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: On the capital allocation front, Leica Biosystems closed the acquisition of StatLab in early Q4.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: StatLab strengthens Leica's value proposition by enabling a more complete pathology workflow, while advancing our integrated delivery network strategy, and helping clinicians diagnose cancer faster and more precisely.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We're very pleased to welcome the StatLab team to Danaher.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Finally, Massimo, our other recent acquisition, continued to track ahead of our initial expectations and delivered another quarter of high single-digit revenue growth.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Having spent time with the team just last week,

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: the integration is progressing well across the business with a healthy funnel of cost savings and commercial synergy opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: The team has also continued to innovate at an impressive pace, recently receiving FDA clearance for its SmartSep platform, that can help detect atrial fibrillation, a common heart rhythm disorder that often goes undetected and significantly increases the risk of stroke.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: This technology can help patients earlier who may benefit from further medical evaluation and care.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: I want to congratulate the Massimo team for their sixth FDA clearance this year and for extending the value of their technology beyond monitoring to help detect important clinical conditions

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: like atrial fibrillation.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And with that, I'll turn the call over to Matt, who will walk you through our Q3 results and guidance in more detail.

sentences.speaker: Management

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: As Julie stated, we delivered a solid third quarter with better-than-expected growth, earnings, and cash flow.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Sales were $6.6 billion, and core growth, excluding respiratory revenue, was up 5.5%.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And encouraging 100 basis points acceleration from the second quarter and a continuation of the improvement we've seen throughout the year.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Respiratory revenue, while slightly better than expected, represented an approximately 250 basis point headwind in the quarter,

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: resulting in core revenue growth of 3%.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Geographically, core revenues in developed markets were flat.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Western Europe grew mid-single digits, and North America was down low single digits, primarily driven by lower respiratory revenue.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Core revenues in high-growth markets increased approximately 10%, with healthy growth across all major regions.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: China was up high single digits, with growth in all three of our segments.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Biotechnology and life sciences were supported by healthier funding, and investment levels and diagnostics continued to move beyond the most significant impacts of China's health care policy changes.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Our gross profit margin for the third quarter was 58.5%.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Our adjusted operating profit margin of 29% was up 110 basis points, and exceeded expectations, driven primarily by strong operational execution, with a modest benefit from tariff refunds received during the quarter.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Adjusted diluted net earnings per common share of $2.11 were up approximately 11.5%.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We generated $1.6 billion of free cash flow in the quarter and $4 billion in the first three quarters of the year, resulting in a year-to-date free cash flow to net income conversion ratio of 128%, further underwriting the debt.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: This is a significant increase in the differentiated quality of our earnings.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Now, turning towards our business segments.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Core revenue in our biotechnology segment increased 5%.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Core revenue in discovery and medical decreased low single digits, with solid growth in protein research instrumentation more than offset by timing and lab consumables.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Core revenue in bioprocessing grew towards the upper end of mid-single digits, modestly better than our expectations.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Consumables were up mid-single digits, led by upstream consumables, while equipment increased low single digits.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Orders grew mid-teens in the quarter, with particular strength in both upstream consumables as well as regits.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: There is no change to our full-year expectation of mid-single digit core revenue growth for bioprocessing.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Demand trends remain healthy across the business,

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: supported by strong commercial production activity and a robust pipeline of new programs.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: These underlying market trends, combined with Cytiva's differentiated portfolio, deep scientific expertise, and recent innovations, reinforce our confidence in the business's ability to deliver sustainable, high single-digit long-term revenue growth, while helping customers improve yields, increase manufacturing efficiency, and scale new therapies.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Core revenue increased 4.5%.

sentences.speaker: Management

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Core revenue in our life sciences instruments businesses

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: increased mid-single digits in the quarter.

sentences.speaker: Management

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Beckman Coulter Life Sciences also delivered strong results, including in automation, where the team has seen increased demand for AI-enabled solutions and services.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Core revenue in our life sciences consumables businesses collectively grew low single digits in the quarter, driven by continued momentum in IDT's MRD and next-generation sequencing product lines, while ABCAM saw improved academic demand and solid traction from pharma

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: and biopharma commercial initiatives.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Now, moving to our diagnostic segment.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Core revenue growth excluding respiratory revenue was up 7%.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Respiratory revenue was an approximately 650 basis point headwind in the quarter, resulting in core revenue growth of 50 basis points.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Core revenue in our clinical diagnostics businesses increased mid-single digits in the quarter.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We saw notable performance at Leica Biosystems, with particular strong momentum in digital pathology as well as advanced staining.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Beckman Coulter Diagnostics also delivered its highest core growth quarter in more than two years.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: The traction we saw from new product introductions, including the DXi 9000,

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: together with easing China policy-related headwinds, reinforces our confidence in Beckman's competitive position and ability to accelerate their growth trajectory.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: In molecular diagnostics, core revenue in Cepheid's non-respiratory business increased low double digits, led by growth in Group A strep, virology, and sexual health assays.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Respiratory revenue was approximately 350 million pieces, down year-over-year due primarily to lower global infection rates, but modestly ahead of our expectations as we saw customers purchase ahead of the upcoming respiratory season.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Now, let's turn to our fourth quarter and full-year 2026 outlook and give you an initial perspective on how we're thinking about 2027.

sentences.text: In the fourth quarter, we expect core revenue growth,

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: excluding respiratory revenue, to be in the 4-5% range.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We expect respiratory revenue to be in the 4-5% range, and we expect core revenue growth to be in the 4-5% range.

sentences.speaker: Management

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Additionally, we expect a fourth quarter adjusted operating profit margin of approximately 29.5%.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: For the full year 2026, we are increasing our full-year adjusted diluted net EPS guidance to $8.57 to $8.62 versus our prior range of $8.45 to $8.60.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: This reflects the benefit of our third quarter and represents double-digit year-over-year EPS growth.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Now, turning to 2027.

sentences.text: While it's still too early to provide a formal outlook, we want to give you some perspective on how we're thinking about core growth next year.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We're encouraged by the improvement in the end markets and the growth we've delivered throughout 2026.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Excluding respiratory revenue, core revenue growth has averaged 4-5% over the past several quarters.

sentences.speaker: Management

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: So, as we look to 2027, we think that 4-5% core revenue growth, excluding respiratory revenue, is the right starting point as we sit today.

sentences.text: We'll provide a more quantitative and detailed guidance outlook in January, but hopefully this gives you a helpful starting point for how we're thinking about next year.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We do use it in certain cases. And particularly one of the places where we're using it quite a bit is in performance marketing. sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: at the moment where we must switch everything to direct payments. That's not currently in

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: the cards. Got it. And as it relates to the record Q3 gross margin, you wouldn't attribute any of that to the growing mix of driving traffic directly to yourself?

sentences.text: No, the main delta in the gross margin was better revenue and less AI costs than we expected

sentences.speaker: Operator
sentences.text: going through. All right. Thank you both. Your next question comes from the line of Ross Sandler with Barclays. Please unmute your audio and video and ask your question.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: Hey guys. Louise, I wanted to go back to the big picture with AI. So we can all see that AI is progressing at a pretty massive clip. The models are getting better. The latency is getting faster. Meta even followed you guys with kind of a sassy avatar launch recently.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: But, you know, the question I have is that like, there's some academic research that says one-on-one tutoring is sort of one of the best ways for anyone to kind of learn a new subject.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: So you talked a little bit earlier about how you're going to integrate some of these,

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: you know, more native AI interactive elements to the app. Right now it's been like kind of an add-on with video, but I'm curious how you're thinking about like the long-term, could these become much more core versus kind of the tap and learn gamified tap and learn use case that we started with at Duolingo? And, you know, how does that change, I guess, the business model for Duolingo as you integrate more of that? Just thoughts on that would be great. Yeah,

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: it's a great question. And when we think about a lot, we know today, you know, a few years ago, maybe four or five years ago, we did a bunch of research that shows that Duolingo was about as good as a classroom for language learning. We've gotten better to the point where I'm pretty sure we're better than a classroom now. But we are today not as good as a one-on-one human tutor.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Nothing has gotten as good as a one-on-one, a good one-on-one human tutor is still better than where we're at now. We think that over the next few years, we will be able to be as good as a one-on-one human tutor because we just see how much we're improving every year. I mean, the thing about one-on-one human tutors is that they're not improving. They're like, it's about as good as we are, but we're improving. So we think we're going to get there.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Now, there's something very important to mention, which is that to a large extent, even though one-on-one human tutors are very effective at teaching, to a large extent, most people don't want to do that. I mean, there's a small fraction of people that are willing to do that, but most people just don't want to, even if it's given out for free.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: It happens that it's not that compelling of an experience on your mobile phone when compared to TikTok or Instagram or whatever. It's just not that compelling. So what we want to do is we want to have something that is as effective as a one-on-one human tutor, and we think we can do it, but it will not look like a one-on-one human tutor. It will, in the end, still feel

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: gamified because ultimately the thing that is most important, even though one-on-one human tutors are very efficient and effective, the thing that is most important, the major failure mode, is people just dropping off. You can have a very effective one-on-one human tutor, but people will be like, yeah, I'm going to stop going to that.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: I'll highlight our momentum across Search, YouTube, and partnerships.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We continue to accelerate the deployment of Gemini models across our market.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We are also expanding our entire ads infrastructure to boost performance in the three areas I've highlighted before.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Ads quality, advertiser tools, and AI user experiences.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: First, ads quality.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: The integration of Gemini models into our ads infrastructure is improving how we decode user intent and drive ads relevance.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: For example, in Q3, we made the biggest update to product listing ads in a decade, adding new AI capabilities to help users make more confident purchase decisions.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Already, we've seen satisfaction increase by 19% and dissatisfaction drop more than half.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We're also seeing AI models enable better prediction of clicks and conversions, stronger overall performance, and deeper personalization of ads.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: For instance, through several innovations and personalization modeling, we delivered 18% incremental advertiser value and an 8% increase in user sentiment on Discover ads in 2026.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Overall, AI is accelerating our ads development and drives the majority of our product launches.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Second, advertiser tools.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We're ensuring every advertiser, from global brands to small businesses, can seamlessly participate in our AI surfaces.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: AI Max and Performance Max continue to see strong adoption.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: To give marketers even more control, we're now introducing a way to test different budgets and ROI targets across multiple Search campaigns in a single AI Max A-B test.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: To drive better performance, we integrated our AI creative tools directly into AI Max.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: In Q3 alone, Gemini models helped advertisers generate over 1.5 billion campaign assets, up over 7x year over year.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: For example, by using AI Max to capture long-form and multilingual queries, Telstra saw a 52% increase in conversions and a 36% reduction in cost per order showing up in key moments however the customers search.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Third, AI user experiences.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Sundar mentioned the distinct behavioral changes we're seeing as users ask entirely new categories of questions.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We think of Search holistically, a unified product spanning traditional results and AI-powered search.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: On AI mode, many of these queries are upper funnel queries, allowing us to capture new high-value commercial intent.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: In addition, the majority of AI mode queries are incremental, creating more monetization opportunities over time.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Additionally, our user research shows that people are comfortable with ads on these surfaces and find them highly relevant.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Click-through rates are already similar between sponsored and organic product list items within AI mode.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Based on these collective results, we're now scaling high-quality ads within AI overviews in AI mode to more users and queries.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: This includes taking our monetization footprint global for the first time.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Today, we're announcing the expansion of ads in AI mode into international markets alongside multi-turn ads in AI mode in the US.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: As always, our approach is deliberate, prioritizing the user experience and engagement first, and then scaling the formats that drive proven ROI for advertisers.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: That discipline is what gives us a strong, durable foundation for the future.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: As Sundar mentioned, we're in the early stages of agentic experiences across our services and excited about the commercial opportunities ahead.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: The universal commerce protocol, UCP, is being rapidly adopted by retailers.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Today, UCP enables direct checkout for hundreds of thousands of brands across Google, including Chewy, Nike, Tapestry, and many more.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We're combining this with the agent payments protocol as we build for the future of commerce.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Our focus spans two fronts, unlocking agentic capabilities that act on behalf of the consumer and designing practical tools that give shoppers confidence and control.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We launched Universal Cart this quarter to support that second track, mirroring how people actually shop today across Google.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: This allows retailers to maintain their relationships with customers while helping to capture sales and avoid abandoned carts.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Moving to YouTube. We view YouTube as a flywheel of creators, viewers, and advertisers.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: First, creators. Every day, more than 20 million videos are being uploaded.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We're making creation easier with new generative AI tools in YouTube Studio, plus a conversational editing assistant in shorts and YouTube Create.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Looking at viewership. At Made on YouTube, we introduce short series where creators can structure their shorts into seasons and episodes.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Sequential playback makes it seamless for viewers to discover new shorts and keep watching.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: The third part is monetization, starting with ads.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Our focus remains on delivering value across the entire funnel.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: They're not only expanding their existing refinery by 100%, which is the largest refinery in the world, they are doubling it.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: They're also putting additional refinery in Kenya. These are all firm projects.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: If you look at their cash flow, it's basically billions of dollars in a quarter. So, these are high certainty projects.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: There are additional investments happening in Africa on petrochemical side too, so we can clearly see that as a trend.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: One thing which we highlighted is also low carbon energy projects are finally taking shape from a low base.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We had two big wins on carbon capture related projects in quarter three, and we have some robust pipeline for quarter four ahead for us. So, there are some investments happening, and the driver for that is European Union continues to hold its mandate for SAF adoption, and to fulfill that demand is more capacity which is required.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Finally, we do see capacity addition for petrochemicals.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Our licensing activity and automation business in petrochemicals continues

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: to remain strong. So, when you add it all together, it's less linked to the oil price. It's more linked to the drivers which are more broader energy security, resiliency, low carbon fuels, or the broader demand of petrochemicals. And that's why we believe it's a multi-year cycle.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: It's less linked to the price. It's more linked to other drivers. That's why it gives us more

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: conviction. Yeah, super helpful, Vimal.

sentences.text: And I guess maybe just to ask Andrew's question slightly differently from before.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: On the refining side of the business, are you seeing any deferral, just given where crack spreads are, refiners maybe running out harder a little bit, given profitability looks really, really good right now. sentences.text: I would say what we all read, deferrals are higher uptime by U.S. refineries is factually correct, which essentially means that some of the activity which requires a shutdown cannot be performed. sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: So, those businesses get protected even though customers are running at a higher rate.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: But there are things which you need to replace, like a Sundyne pump has to be replaced, you need a shutdown.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Or if you want to refurbish

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: a catalyst. So, to me, there's some demand moving right, but it's not a lost demand, it's moving, it's kind of pent up demand which will eventually show up. But when you look at the global view, the overall services and catalyst demand is very stable.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: As I mentioned before, we see the catalyst demand to be in high teens in quarter four.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Next year, we see overall catalysts to be very stable.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: With single digit growth services, growth remains very stable.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: So, yeah, absolutely, this is a trend of high utilization and no shutdowns.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: But it doesn't change the overall dynamics of the business for us in the near term.

sentences.text: Thank you, very helpful.

sentences.text: Thanks, Joe.

sentences.text: Thank you. Our next question comes from the line of Varun Gurindaraj with Bernstein. Please proceed with your question.

sentences.text: Good morning, everyone. Thanks for the question.

sentences.text: Sure, good morning.

sentences.text: So, question on PAT. When you're looking at projects and their delivery times, have they been in line with historical norms? I think there's been a concern that we're short labor in North America and that might lead to some of this just getting stretched.

sentences.text: Are you seeing any of that in your numbers or is that not really a concern right now?

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Not a concern because a large part of our backlog is actually not in North America.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: LNG backlog is in North America.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Everything else is in the rest of the world.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And in case of LNG, we build our own equipment in our own factory and we have enough capacity to fulfill all the backlogs, so we don't have any concern on that. On a broader basis, the construction labor or labor shortages is a trend, but that's not driving any impact on our revenue execution on a visible basis.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: Appreciate it. Thank you.

sentences.speaker: Operator
sentences.text: Your line is open.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: Thank you.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: Jamie and Jeremy, you guys have talked about, you've seen some excesses in underwriting and credit late last year, I think it was Jamie.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: Jeremy, you talked about risk on in the capital markets.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: What are you guys seeing in credit underwriting from your competitors?

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: Is it getting crazier or no?

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: It's still pretty good.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: And what's the outlook there, please?

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: I mean, crazy is a strong word, but, you know, I spent some time looking into this issue like a week ago.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And, you know, we did hear some example.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: I mean, I don't know, for whatever reason, I think the data center underwriting space is one that resonates with me as a kind of bellwether for what people are doing.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And, you know, we passed on some deals that, you know, obviously, because when you look at the data center stuff, the key question is like, what happens with power supply?

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: What happens with tenants?

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: What happens with, you know, it's a well-discussed thing.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And we have a pretty precise framework to govern what we're willing to do and what we're not willing to do in that space across those types of risks.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And we saw some deals come through where,

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: you know, we were just like, yeah, we're not doing that.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: So, you know, it's normal, I guess.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: It's competitive and people are eager to be involved.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And, you know, in some cases, there's ironically some element of like relationship lending that's happening through the data center space when it's kind of a startup entity that's building the data center.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: So that's part of the story a little bit too.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: But I don't think we're screaming from the rooftops that, you know, underwriting is underwriting center to center collapse.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: But I think you see normal pressures and we're navigating those in the way that we do, which is, you know, we do flex in some moments for particularly important clients

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: in situations where we feel like it's the right and a kind of appropriately skeptical view of- A huge deterioration, very mild one, but it's across, you know, people, assumptions on revenue growth or add back of expenses, more pick, weaker, some weaker, and this is not across the board, it's more some players than others, you know, some weaker governance, some people taking more rollover up

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: to how much interest, but it is across that spectrum you've seen, trying to make it weigh your credit cycle, how will everybody perform?

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And I don't think it's gonna be like a bell curve of performance, by the way, in the great financial crisis.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: I totally agree with you, Jamie, on that.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: I don't wanna sound Pollyannaish, but on a question regarding the regulatory outlook, obviously we've got Basel III end game, hopefully we've been codified maybe by the end of the year, I know you guys have put out your remarks on it, and next year, hopefully we get tailoring.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: Could you envision a period where, and again, I don't wanna sound Pollyannaish, but a period where the regulators are just set, where you go, because the last 20 years has been constant change with the regulators affecting the banking industry.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: Could we enter a period where we have a stability in the regulatory environment,

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: which could enhance valuations possibly for bank stocks?

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Well, go ahead, I know.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: I would break the question down into two parts, like could we envision stability and impact on valuations?

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: On the question of stability, I mean, I don't think it's Pollyannaish to say that regulatory stability is a desirable thing, and I actually think it's a relatively non-partisan idea.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: In the meantime, we're not going to allow just any agent to come, you know, outside agent to come in inside the company because it's just too risky for clients and for Jake and Morgan.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: That's good color.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: And just separately, I think as we assess the risk of interest rates, maybe moving even higher than what we saw in the third quarter, maybe your latest thoughts around how you assess the resiliency of the economy to handle maybe a 6% rate on tenure and just the fed hiking a few times.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: Do you think the risk of a market event or just stress on the economy is meaningful as we, as we kind of discount that?

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: I think you have to, we always prepare for all different events, you know, and that's not the same as predicting them because we want to be a strong company, helping our clients, our communities, countries around the world, the sick or thin.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: So of course things like that can happen.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: I would never take it off the table and they can happen for good reason, which is a lot of demand for capital, a lot of productivity and things are fine, you can have a bad reason, you know, in thinking inflation around the world, they can happen not because it's in the United States, you have, because what happens overseas.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: So not predicting it.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: You know, I've always thought there's a higher chance of other people.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: I still kind of think that, but there's not a prediction that's just a, because that is cautious preparation.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Thank you.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Thank you.

sentences.speaker: Operator
sentences.text: Our next question comes from John McDonald with Truist.

sentences.speaker: Operator
sentences.text: Your line is open.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: Hi, good morning, Jeremy and Jamie.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: Was hoping Jeremy, you could unpack the new outlook for 2027 and AI, the central case that you gave, including some of the assumptions around the balance sheet growth, deposit pricing and the impact of higher rates.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Yeah, sure.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: John, no problem.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: So if you start with what we've given you as the AIX markets guide for fourth quarter, which is 25 and a half, and you annualize that, you get something like 102.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: So we're essentially giving you, you know, guiding to 5 billion of growth from that to the 107.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: That 5 billion, probably about a quarter of that, I would say, is related to the yield curve.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: So we remain, you know, asset sensitive and probably a little bit more asset sensitive than the EAR shows just because of the lower than modeled deposit betas.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: So, you know, about a quarter of that is the hikes that are, that are currently in the forward curve.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: I think there's one in December and then two through the first half of the year.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And the rest of it, I would actually describe pretty straightforwardly as just a continuation of the balance sheet growth and mixed trends that you've seen this year.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: So both continued, you know, modest consumer deposit growth, continued wholesale deposit growth, probably a wholesale a bit weaker than what was very strong this year, but we don't actually know.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And then card loans, which obviously can be a big driver of NII, continue.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Actually a pretty straightforward caveat, but you know, I gave you the caveat on the prepared remuneration.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: I mean, I mean, I think there's more uncertainty around that number than normal because of all the things going on around the world.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And obviously it also relates to what we do, which we can change at any point in time.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: Okay.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: That's awful.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: Thank you.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: And Jeremy on expenses, if we move over to there, do you have any preliminary thoughts on your investment spend plan for next year?

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: The other drivers of expenses and how those might line up with the current street forecast for expenses next year?

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Um, yeah.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: So, um, you know, we try to draw a little bit of a distinction between NII and expenses in the sense that, you know, despite Jamie's comments, which are obviously true that we can modify, you know, the structure of the balance sheet to change the NII in general, undisturbed, the NII is kind of a property of the balance sheet at a given point in time.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And it's not that sensitive, um, to the budget cycle.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And therefore we feel like we don't have a very good excuse at this point in the year for pretending that we don't have an opinion about 2027.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Expenses are a little different in the sense that they are still sensitive to the budget cycle.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And there are a lot of discretionary decisions to get made in there.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And while we have some preliminary views, we're kind of not done with that.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And you will remember, obviously, John, last year we did point out that

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: our preliminary read on expenses suggested that the market's consensus was a bit off.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: That seems to be quite a bit less true this year.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: So we see the consensus right now for 2027 expenses being around 114 billion and our current preliminary read isn't too far from that.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: So kind of no news on that front, I would say.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And let's see, you know, how the budget cycle finishes and, you know, as Jamie points out, I think the uncertainty isn't just about the macro environment, it's also about how dynamic the investment picture is and the effects of AI, et cetera, et cetera, et cetera.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: So a lot of moving parts, but for now, the consensus doesn't.

sentences.speaker: Operator
sentences.text: Thank you.

sentences.speaker: Operator
sentences.text: Our next question comes from Erica Nazarian with UBS.

sentences.speaker: Operator
sentences.text: Your line is open.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: Yes, thank you.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: Good morning.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: Um, my first question just is on capital management.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: You know, we were fielding a lot of inbound questions from investors in terms of the billion dollar buyback versus, you know, the normal cadence of around 7 billion.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: And I know that there's no normal cadence and I know that buyback is the last priority.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: Um, but perhaps, you know, take us through how you should think.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: We should think about your capital priorities, particularly given that we're hearing that Basel three end game and GSIB should be finalized at year end.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Yeah.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: So I think we've told you all that we have probably 30 billion or something of excess capital rush roughly just estimating what all the end games are, which we don't know, but that's plenty.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: But the capital hierarchy has always been the same.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And we'll disclose that and do some work on it.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: But I guess it'll be considerably more than that.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And the world needs capital.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: The world needs advice.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: The world is becoming more complex.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Uh, you know, assets and management around the world are bigger.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And so we think that's good.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We think that's good news in the long run.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And we can't tell you what it means, you know, for the next six months, but, uh, that's why we're doing it.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We hope to deploy it very well for our shareholders.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Yeah.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And the only thing I would add to that, Erica, is just that if you notice what the journey has been on the C2-1 ratio, I want to say that we started at something like 15-7 and we're now at 13-9 during a period during which we've done a ton of internal deployment.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: So there's been a lot of organic growth and the RWA and some of the investments that Jamie alludes to.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Um, and during that period, we've also, also done a bunch of buybacks.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: So, but at this point, you know, we're, we're, as Jamie says, it, you know,

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: the, the, the speed with which we've been able to deploy organically relative to the amount of access that we have and the environment seems pretty clear that it makes sense to keep drive out.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: I want to brag on the investment bank a little bit, but they've hired a tremendous amount of very talented people at SRI.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And we're lucky to have Todd Combs here, you know, investing some of the capital.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: They've had a lot of ideas.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: It's not just meetings at this point.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: They've helped fund some interesting types of things.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We have more ideas.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: They're doing a really great policy around it too, which is what, what can you do to accelerate, you know, security resilience United States around, you know, what's chip building or, and we had a big announcement in Philadelphia.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Uh, so I, I just, I'm proud of them.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: You know, we've had a bunch of people who retired, who raised a hand.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: They're coming back, you know, more for patients than anything else.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And so, uh, it's been just a great effort for the company.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And as we pointed out, it's global and the global response has also been exceptional.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: I have something across my desk, which is alone, you know, over 10 or $20 billion of financing, uh, in one country.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: So, uh, uh, a lot more to come here.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And I would put the same category of American dream initiative, the innovation economy initiative, uh, the commercial banking initiative around the world, these things are working.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Uh, we think we're doing the right kind of good business at good returns.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: So as a follow up here, that all sounds, um, you know, um, very positive for activity levels going forward in a very broad way.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: And Jamie, I know that you did some media over the past few weeks and talked about the pipeline.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: And maybe in that context, especially given market fears that the bond market route around the world, it has a chilling effect on activity levels.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: Maybe talk about what the pipeline looks like for activity levels in both, uh, you know, the investment and both quote, wall street and main street.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Well, first before I do that, the bond volatility, the market, the fear is not going to change what we do.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We serve clients with sick or thin.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We know that I call some of the economic wins.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: It's the weather.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: That's not exactly referred to the pipeline is fine.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: No, but I pointed out many times before the pipeline is like an accordion, it could open closed pretty quick.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: You've seen in the United States has been built.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: I, as Jeremy says, the word delayed, probably we don't really know when you will see, but I was in Europe recently and the pipeline there is actually quite healthy and even more so in IPOs than we would have thought.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: So, uh, we just don't know.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And it's serving the clients and doing a good job is the most important thing.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: No pipelines.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We always forecast the pipeline.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: It's called the probability.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Probably.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And we know, and we know one thing for sure.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: It'll be wrong.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Like when Jamie and I talk about not knowing, I think we mean we don't obviously know exactly what investment banking fee revenue is going to be in the fourth quarter.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: I think that we do know that the overall environment is robust and supportive.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And there's a lot of business that wants to get done and needs to get done.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And as you point out, Erika, not surprisingly, given the rate sell off, you're going to have the market take a little bit of a breath and a pause to make sure buyers and sellers can meet on valuation terms.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And so we did see a little bit of that slowdown and, you know, the second half of September, basically.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And we'll see how that plays out in December, but I mean, sorry,

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: but the big picture, I think, is pretty clear.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Thank you.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Thank you.

sentences.speaker: Operator
sentences.text: Our next question comes from Chris McGrady with KBW.

sentences.speaker: Operator
sentences.text: Your line is open.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: Oh, great.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: Thanks.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: Just following up on the capital allocation, maybe a comment or two on where you're less comfortable allocating capital to.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: It seems like there's plenty of opportunities to deploy.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: Where are you pulling back?

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: Where are you seeing structures or peers maybe doing something you may not want to do?

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: Thank you.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: I'm not going to give you very specific stuff, but we're tightening up a little bit on credit.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: I think some of the credit terms are kind of a little bit loose.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And you've heard us talk about that before and other people, you know, a little too much pay, a little too weak governance, a little too much priming, good assets, a little too much pushing on it.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: You know, we just don't feel like we have to chase that kind of stuff anymore.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: Great.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: And then secondarily, the health of the consumer is getting a lot of attention.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: I guess the question is durability to withstand these kind of rates.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: I think you talked about 10% year on year spend and debit and credit.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: If we're a year from now and we still have rates where we are, what's your expectation for the ability for the consumer to hold on?

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: Thanks.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: I mean, you know, obviously if you keep real rates very, very high for a long time at some level, you know, that's designed to slow down economic activity to fight inflation.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And it's hard to imagine that that wouldn't have an impact on the consumer.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: So far, what we see in the current data and what's been true, I would say, for the last few years, the consumer has been quite resilient in the face of a number of headwinds that under different circumstances, you might have expected would present a challenge.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: It's what counts as HQLA to start with.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: How you do LCR, I think they should look at all that, because with the view that I think you can create safer banks with more deployed capital and more liquidity you can use to intermediate markets.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And that should be the goal, but it's hard to answer the question, because this is gonna be up to them.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Either way, J-Mobile will serve our clients and do a good job, take care of, do what we're supposed to do, but I think they should be doing that.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: So we'll see.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We don't have to speculate what they're gonna do.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: There are a lot of proposals out there,

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: as far as international rules, but I applaud them for looking at it.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Yeah, now I think that I agree with everything Jamie said, and it's really particularly complicated across a range of dimensions.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: I will note that at Company Update, we actually talked about this, and in some sense kind of gave you the answer, because what we said at the time was that the problem with the situation where the system has a healthy amount of capital but it's relatively constrained, is that just at the margin, it leads you to have your asset deployment be in much higher risk density instruments, essentially.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And so a place where you're a little bit more balanced would tend to move you towards lower risk density, and it just enables you to serve a broader part of the economy,

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: including mortgages, consumer lending, also some of the more secured C&I type structures.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: I was gonna say, if they wanna reduce the size of the Fed balance sheet, they're gonna have to make some changes.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Got it, thank you.

sentences.speaker: Operator
sentences.text: Thank you, our next question comes from Matt O'Connor with Deutsche Bank, your line is open.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: Good morning, I was hoping you could talk more about how the growing non-interest-bearing deposits when a number of peers aren't, and then just how you're thinking about that specific buck or deposits in a higher rate environment if you can continue to grow.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Yeah, I mean, I think I've sort of addressed that point to some degree in connection with, I think my answer to John's question on the 2027 NIO book and how we're feeling about consumer deposit growth, but I guess just to reiterate a couple of points, like number one, our net new checking account growth has been exceptionally strong, 650,000 supporters, so people are reacting, they're responding well to the marketing, they're responding well to the brand, the value proposition, to the sort of multi-decade investment and the product bundle that we offer our consumers.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: So I think that's really good news and has been a contributor to the kind of reassertion of consumer deposit growth.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: As I noted, the question a little bit

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: in this rate hiking cycle is going to be how those balances behave and how pricing pressure behaves and how much migration we see to higher beta products and so on.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And we'll see.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: I think we're relatively optimistic right now and we wouldn't expect radical changes for like small local moves, but we do think a lot about the different rate regimes and how that can affect deposit data.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: I think that's part of the spring.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: Okay, and I guess I was thinking more specifically the non-interest-bearing deposits, which I think are more kind of in the commercial corporate side of things.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: So I was just trying to see if there's any color there in terms of like cash management products, you know, things that have been a key driver.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: The cash, most of the non-interest barriers is consumer, and that's because we're growing the business and you have different products for different types of consumers.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And I think the wholesale side, commercial is much more competitive than that.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Yeah, no, I think to be honest, the reporting is a little confusing in part because of the famous ECR product that sometimes makes it look like on the wholesale side there are more non-interest.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: You want a bit more color on that, Matt.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: You can say that wholesale deposits have been, continue to be, and in fact, at the margin are a little bit more.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: The way to think about that is not that

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: the product offering allows us to grow an overall margin that you earn on your deposit or your service offering is, and we have quite a good track record there.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: I understand, thank you.

sentences.speaker: Operator
sentences.text: Thank you.

sentences.speaker: Operator
sentences.text: Our next question comes from David Chevarini with Jeffreys, your line is open.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: Hi, thanks for taking the question.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: So JP Morgan's ROTC target through the cycle is 17% versus the 21% today.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: Is there anything you're seeing either in the macro environment or competitive environment that could accelerate a path to 17% or is that not anywhere on the horizon?

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: I've always talked about the 17% being through the cycle.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Times are pretty good now with high volume and high asset prices and fairly low credit losses and all that.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: So if you can earn 17% consistently for a long period of time, that's a really good return for shareholders.

sentences.speaker: Management
