sentences.text: Following the encouraging improvement in the U.S. trends through the quarter post the interventions that you noted, can you touch a little bit more on how you're thinking about that U.S. sales trajectory over the balance of this year and any high-level thoughts to share on the path into 27 as you think about the benefits from the interventions and the benefits from next? Thank you.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Good morning, Dennis. It's Ian. Let me maybe start, and then I'll let Chris chime in maybe at the end. And the results that we've seen in Q3 are all kind of conflicted.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: I think we're in a position to be confirmatory to what we outlined there, which was that our focus was about how we got the U.S. business in a stronger position as we exit 2026.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: I think certainly we feel really good about the work and the decisions that Sky and the U.S. system collectively are putting into place.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: I think we're, as you heard us say in our upfront remarks, we're encouraged by the baseline traffic trends that we've seen through September and now through October. And I think we remain really confident that the U.S. is on the right path to exit 2026 in a stronger position.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: I might just also touch on IOM because I'm sure that's a question that's coming.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And I just would say with IOM, I think as we outlined in our opening remarks, see in almost the majority of our large international markets, we're holding or gaining share.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: It's a soft consumer environment, but we're doing well.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And I think our international markets are very consistently executing that playbook of menu marketing and value.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: I think to be largely consistent through the rest of the year.

sentences.speaker: Operator
sentences.text: Over to JP Morgan.

sentences.speaker: Operator
sentences.text: Hi, thank you.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: So I have had an opportunity to visit a fully operational next door with hand-breaded chicken.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And I will tell you, I'm very impressed to kind of see that operating in person.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: The point of the question is, when I look at...

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: The hand-breaded chicken platform, does it make more sense to maybe just pursue significant upgrades of the sandwich, of the strip, for example, as part of hand-breading and maybe pursue those type of product categories versus going into what I think might just be a higher risk category with bone in wings?

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And I do ask the bone in wing question in the context of the Mighty Wing kind of experience

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: of 10 years ago.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Is there something significant maybe that we could have learned from that in terms of the ease of execution of that product?

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Thank you so much.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We're doing in there and we've got in looking at two experience and feedback on restaurants, but we're seeing that wings provides really strong incrementality.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Again, it's in those 10 restaurants, it's really early, but that's an interesting learning.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: So I think we're in kind of the now, how do we actually go about and execute whether there's...

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Maybe the only hook, John, just looking at the...

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Okay.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: I think I'm kind of confident that there may be some nuances market to market in that, but we certainly have had success with wings in a number of markets globally.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Good afternoon.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: My name is Krista, and I'll be your conference operator today.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: At this time, I would like to welcome everyone to Metta's third quarter, 2026 earnings conference call.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: All lines have been placed on mute to prevent any background noise.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: After the speaker's remarks, there'll be a question and answer session.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: If you would like to ask a question, please press star one on your telephone keypad.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: To withdraw your question, again, press star one.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We ask that you limit yourself to one question, and this call will be recorded.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Thank you very much.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Rob Bevegni, Metta's Director of Investor Relations, you may begin.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Thank you.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Good afternoon, and welcome to Metta platform's

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: third quarter, 2026 earnings conference call.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Joining me today to discuss our results are Mark Zuckerberg, CEO, and Susan Lee, CFO.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Our remarks today will include forward-looking statements, which are based on assumptions as of today.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Act for results may differ materially as a result of various factors, including those set forth in today's earnings press release, and in our quarterly report on Form 10Q filed with the SEC.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We undertake no obligation to update any forward-looking statement.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: During this call, we will present both GAAP and certain non-GAAP financial measures.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: A reconciliation of GAAP to non-GAAP measures is included in today's earnings press release.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: The earnings press release and an accompanying investor presentation are available on our website at investor.atmetta.com.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And now I'd like to turn the call over to Mark.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: All right, hey everyone, thanks for joining today.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: This has been a busy and exciting few months.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Our family of apps is now used by 3.64 billion people each day, and we are seeing all time highs and engagement on both Facebook and Instagram, driven by strong growth in video.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Threads has now overtaken X in monthly actives and continues to grow quickly.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: WhatsApp is hitting all time highs in messaging and is becoming an increasingly important platform for agents as well.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: In the last few months, we have had several major milestones towards our goal of delivering personal super intelligence to everyone.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We had one of our most successful launches ever with the Muse personal agent.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We shipped Muse Wonder as our first frontier model, and we shipped several new glasses and gadgets with Muse integration, including coming soon to our new audio glasses.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We've been discussing our vision for personal super intelligence for more than a year now.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We wanna help every person have an extremely capable personal agent that understands their goals and can help you achieve them and improve your life in whatever ways you want, whether that's improving your relationships, helping you save time, save money, build a business, create new things, or anything else that you can dream of.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Muse is the product form of this vision.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: So now we have the foundational technology in place to deliver this.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: There is still a lot of work ahead,

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: but our initial position is very strong.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: In just a month and a half, more than 10 million people in the US and Canada have set up Muse personal agents.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Growth continues to be strong, and we have been number one in the app store almost every day.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Engagement and retention are also off to a strong start.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: About 25% of people who have set up Muse use it on any given day.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: For our earliest adopters, the longer that they use Muse, the better that retention seems to get.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: So to put this in perspective, this is more than twice the level that Threads started at or where we believe that other AI apps started at as well.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: The most common use case for Muse is shopping.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: With more than a quarter of people who are using Muse engaging in this with an average purchase size of over $200, Plaid told us that they hadn't seen activity like they're seeing with their connector on any other service before.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And in the first week, we had to work with Stripe to raise credit limits since the volumes were above what any of us expected.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Beyond shopping, the most common connectors are for personal productivity and connecting Muse to your other services like email and calendar.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Now this shows the importance of the Muse secure VM that we've built to provide state of the art privacy and security.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And we're looking forward to following up soon with the Muse confidential VM, which will make it so that even meta cannot see your content.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We've also seen that Muse wonder improves quality, engagement and retention further, which suggests that as we continue to improve intelligence, Muse will perform better and better over time.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Now that Muse has clear product market fit, we are entering a new phase and a more operational phase that is focused on scaling it.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: The goals for this next phase will play to many of Meta's strengths.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We need to do three things, scale the product, grow revenue and optimize compute costs.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We expect to grow Muse to serve billions of people.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: This is both our mission and our strategy.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: It's our mission in that we believe in putting the power of personal super intelligence in everyone's hands.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We believe that that is the path to ensuring a positive future for everyone with individual empowerment, empowerment as the source of prosperity and balance of power is the foundation for safety.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: On a values level, we believe that delivering this capability widely is the best thing that we can be doing.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: This is also our strategy because we think that billions of Muses in a network at scale will be able to get more done for people and businesses by working together.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: So we'd like to create a large scale Muse network as quickly as possible.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: From a business perspective, the average revenue per American user for our existing Muse users is, sorry for our existing family of apps users

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: is several hundreds of dollars annually.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And we expect that Muse will reach an even higher level over time due to the amount of commerce that we already see taking place.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Alongside growth, we are focused on building sustainable unit economics.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Muse's compute intensity means that expanding its user base will require significant investment, and we expect total serving costs to rise.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: At the same time, we expect to improve compute cost efficiency by more than tenfold over the next year, driven by better utilization

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: of off-peak capacity, more efficient models, and inference optimization.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: As revenue scales, these efficiency gains give us confidence in our ability to build a highly profitable business over time.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Moving now to our financial outlook.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We expect fourth quarter 2026 total revenue to be in the range of $73 to $76 billion.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Our guidance assumes foreign currency is an approximately 1% headwind to year-over-year total revenue growth based on current exchange rates.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Turning to the expense and CapEx outlooks.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We are raising our expense outlook to incorporate the $9.9 billion charge related to legal proceedings recognized in Q3.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We now expect full year 2026 total expenses to be in the range of $175 to $179 billion.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Excluding the Q3 legal charge, we continue to expect 2026 operating income to be above 2025 operating income.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: At a segment level, we now expect Reality Labs losses to decline compared to 2025 to a range of $18 to $19 billion.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We anticipate 2026 capital expenditures including principal payments on finance leases to be in the range of $135 to $145 billion narrowed from our prior outlook of $130 to $145 billion.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Absent any changes to our tax landscape, we expect our fourth quarter 2026 tax rate to be between 15 and 17%.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Additionally, we continue to monitor active legal and regulatory matters that could significantly impact our business and financial results.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: For example, we continue to see scrutiny on youth related issues in several markets and have a number of youth related trials scheduled in the coming months in the United States.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Looking beyond 2026, we are still developing our budget and capacity plans for next year, but we expect to continue investing aggressively to support both our core business and emerging AI initiatives.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Our current capacity and what is scheduled to come online

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: gives us the flexibility to allocate resources across model training, core business growth, and the development and support of new products.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Our AI investments are already delivering substantial incremental advertising revenue through stronger engagement, better recommendations, and more efficient monetization.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Building on this progress, our MSL investments are creating the technology and infrastructure needed to unlock significant new revenue opportunities and strengthen capabilities across the business.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: While these investments will take longer to generate returns than those in our core business, the breadth of monetization opportunities and internal efficiencies gives us confidence in their long-term potential.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Looking ahead, although we are not providing

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: a full year 2027 revenue outlook, the benefits our AI investments are delivering to the core business, combined with emerging opportunities from model advances and product launches, position us to sustain strong overall revenue growth throughout 2027.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Separately, we remain focused on improving Reality Lab's profitability.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: As Mark mentioned, we expect losses to narrow next year to around $15 billion as we reallocate investment towards other priority areas, primarily AI.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Finally, today we announced plans to create a new class of non-voting capital stock, which will be distributed to all existing shareholders through a stock dividend.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: For each existing share held,

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: stockholders will receive one share of the new non-voting stock, effectively resulting in a two-for-one stock split.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We expect trading to begin in late January 2027.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Enclosing our business momentum continued in Q3 with strong execution across our core ads and engagement initiatives, and we're also excited by our progress towards bringing personal superintelligence to everyone.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: With that, Christa, let's open up the call for questions.

sentences.speaker: Operator
sentences.text: We will now open the lines for a question and answer session.

sentences.speaker: Operator
sentences.text: To ask a question, please press star one on your touchtone phone.

sentences.speaker: Operator
sentences.text: To withdraw your question, you may press star one again.

sentences.speaker: Operator
sentences.text: Please limit yourself to one question.

sentences.speaker: Operator
sentences.text: Please pick up your handset before asking your question to ensure clarity.

sentences.speaker: Operator
sentences.text: If you were streaming today's call, please mute your computer speakers.

sentences.speaker: Operator
sentences.text: And your first question comes from the line of Brian Nowak with Morgan Stanley.

sentences.speaker: Operator
sentences.text: Please go ahead.

sentences.speaker: Operator
sentences.text: Thanks for taking my questions.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: I have two, one on Muse, one on Enterprise.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: Maybe I first congrats on the success of Muse.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: But as you analyze the user behavior and the product, can you talk with us a little bit about any of the constraints to the slope of forward user growth that you're most focused on addressing, whether it's capabilities, model efficiency, capacity, et cetera, just so we understand what are the limiting factors to forward user growth that you want to address.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: And the second one is on Enterprise.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: Mark, can you just walk us through your presentation and your vision for the Meta Enterprise product offering and the key value drivers you hope to provide for the enterprise adopting the service?

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Yeah, I think I can talk about both of those.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And then Susan can jump in with anything else.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: All right, so right now for Muse, we are, one of the things I pointed out is we have more than 10 million people in the US and Canada who have set it up.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: As a reminder, this call is being recorded Tuesday, October 20, 2026.

sentences.speaker: Operator
sentences.text: I would now like to turn the call over to Chinmay Trivedi, Senior Vice President of Investor Relations and Financial Planning and Analysis at 3M.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Thank you. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to our Quarterly Earnings Conference Call.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: With me today are Bill Brown, 3M's Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, and Anurag Maheshwari, 3M's Chief Financial Officer.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Bill and Anurag will make some formal comments, then we will take your questions.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Please note that today's earnings release and slide presentation accompanying this call are posted on the homepage of our Investor Relations website at 3M.com.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Please turn to slide 2 and take a moment to read the forward-looking statements.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: During today's conference call, we'll be making certain predictive statements that reflect our current views about 3M's future performance and financial results.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: These statements are for the 3M Financial Relations website.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: These statements are based on certain assumptions and expectations of future events that are subject to risks and uncertainties.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Item 1A of our most recent Form 10Q lists some of the most important risk factors that could cause actual results to differ from our predictions.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Please note, throughout today's presentation, we'll be making references to certain non-GAAP financial measures.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Reconciliations of the non-GAAP measures can be found in the attachments to today's press release.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: With that, please turn to slide 3 and I will hand the call off to Bill.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Bill?

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Thank you, Chinmay, and good morning, everyone.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We delivered strong performance in Q3, including organic growth of 3.3%,

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: operating margin of 26.2%, up 110 basis points, earnings per share of $2.50, up 12%, and free cash flow of $1.2 billion.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We returned $600 million to shareholders in the past year, including $400 million in dividends and $200 million of share repurchases.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: These results include Madison Fire and Rescue, which is now fully consolidated into our financial reporting and reflect a change in acquisition amortization reporting.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Our updated guidance for the year incorporates both items, and OnRog will provide additional details later in the call.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Based on our Q3 performance and continued strong order trends,

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: we remain transparent.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We are confident in achieving organic growth of greater than 3.5% this year.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: The progress we're delivering reflects the disciplined execution of the strategy we've been implementing over the last two years.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: As we've discussed, a value creation framework is centered around three phases, building the foundation, driving transformation, and accelerating performance.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Our results today are clear evidence that we're making progress across all three.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We're strengthening the foundation, and we're building critical capabilities to position 3M for long-term success.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We've invested in Salesforce effectiveness and AI-enabled tools.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We've sharpened our focus on priority verticals where we can win, and improved how we allocate R&D resources.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Operationally, we're delivering on our goals to improve productivity, quality, and supply chain performance.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: In the quarter, we launched 87 new products, up 24%, and we're on track to exceed our target of 350 this year.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Year-to-date, five-year new product sales are up 34% versus last year to nearly $3 billion, resulting in new product vitality in the mid-teens from a low of 11% in 2024.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Cross-selling is also gaining traction, with $140 million in wins booked to date,

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: and another $120 million in the pipeline, well ahead of our original target, which is $1.5 billion.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And in today's higher inflation environment, our price execution has been particularly strong, and fully offsets material and oil cost pressures.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Across our manufacturing and supply chain network, productivity improvements including procurement savings, higher asset utilization from increased throughput and lower downtime, and improved quality drove gross margins up 230 basis points year-over-year.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Cost support quality improved by 40 basis points, and overall equipment effectiveness improved by 20 basis points.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We continue to see meaningful opportunities to further simplify and standardize, reshape the portfolio, reduce risk, and improve enterprise resilience and predictability.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We've closed 16 manufacturing sites and distribution centers year-to-date, and are taking action on 10 more over the next 12 months, supporting further gross margin improvement beyond 2027.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And the Madison Fire and Rescue acquisition, which is now combined with our SCBA business and reported as a separate division within SIPG, is off to a good start.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: The JV delivered high single-digit pro forma growth, and operating margins ahead of our deal model and 3M overall,

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: and integration is well underway to capture synergies across distribution, international expansion, and operational performance.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And we continue our efforts to address litigation risk, and are actively working with a court-appointed mediator for the AFFF Personal Injury MDL, and more information is available in our quarterly filing.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Moving to slide 4, I'll provide a bit more color on our end market performance.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We continue to see strong momentum in general industrial and safety, with second half growth accelerating to high single digits, above our prior expectations.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Space materials is a great example how we can take differentiated 3M technologies, and extend them into entirely new markets.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: As shown on the left side of the slide, we're combining our capabilities in films, adhesives, and others, to solve light, thermal, energy, and weight challenges across multiple parts of a spacecraft, from the satellite chassis to solar arrays.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Our current pipeline supports opportunities from low earth to geosynchronous orbits, and across a range of commercial and government customers.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: In Q3, we launched a lightweight reflective film for a commercial constellation to reduce light scattering toward earth, and address light pollution concerns.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And we plan to launch another product in Q4 to provide a moisture resistant barrier for solar panels.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We have more than 10 other projects in development or in pre-pipeline stage that will follow in the next few years.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And on the right side of the slide, there's been a lot of interest in expanded beam optics, and the opportunity ahead of us.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And in light of an AK filing and press release last evening, I wanted to take a minute, to highlight the progress we're making.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: As a reminder, EBO's patented FERAL technology enables faster installation, greater durability, and higher density optical connections for AI infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: The technology is particularly valuable in scale out and scale across applications, including optical backplanes, where connectors at the back of a server rack can be difficult to access, install, and maintain.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We previously announced a partnership and deployment with Microsoft, and said we were also engaged in proof of concept work with five additional global hyposcalers,

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: one of whom was Amazon Web Services.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Last evening, we filed an AK stating we issued a warrant to Amazon to purchase up to 3.2 million shares, or approximately 0.6% of 3M common stock, based upon the achievement of $6 billion in cumulative sales of optical connectors, and other data center-related products over the next seven years, and other event-based milestones.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We also announced that we signed a contract manufacturing agreement with Genius Electronic Optical Company, or GSEO, and acquired a 4.7% stake in the company in a private placement to cement our strategic partnership.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: GSEO is a credible and proven supplier of premium consumer device components, and they will help us rapidly advance technology development and scale EBO manufacturing on top of our internal capacity expansion plans.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: But as we previously said, success in this space requires building a robust ecosystem of partners.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We're actively supporting industry standardization through the EBO Multi-Source Agreement, which started with 17 members and is now up to 63.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: This MSA brings together hyperscalers, connectivity providers, and chip designers under a common framework to establish industry standards and certify practitioners.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: EBO was highlighted by many of these ecosystem partners at last week's Open Compute Project Global Summit, including by one other hyperscaler demonstrating EBO in a next-gen rack design running live traffic, and it was headlined in a recent article by Semi Analysis, a well-respected trade journal.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We believe the combination of industry collaboration through the MSA, growing ecosystem adoption, and differentiated 3M know-how positions us well to benefit as EBO becomes a larger part of next-generation AI infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Overall, we've made meaningful progress in reinvigorating our innovation engine over the last two years.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Success requires speed and precise execution, and we're building a stronger, faster, more innovative, and more resilient 3M.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: As this company-wide effort evolves, I'm confident it will translate into faster growth, higher margins, and stronger free cash flow over time.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: With that, I'll turn it over to Anurag to share the details of the quarter.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Anurag?

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Thank you, Bill.

sentences.speaker: Management

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And we expect some more here in the fourth quarter.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: So just a little extra color there.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Thank you.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: You're welcome.

sentences.speaker: Operator
sentences.text: Thank you.

sentences.speaker: Operator
sentences.text: The last question comes from the line of Ken Herbert of RBC Capital Markets.

sentences.speaker: Operator
sentences.text: Please go ahead, Ken.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: Yeah, hi, good morning.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: Thanks for squeezing me in.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: As you look at the strong aftermarket growth in Pratt, you've obviously talked a lot about the GTF strength.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: How much of that growth was GTF, and can you give us any more update on what you're seeing on PW4, V25, and maybe Pratt Canada aftermarket in the quarter?

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Thanks, Ken.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Listen, the majority of that growth came from the GTF aftermarket.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We're still seeing really solid content on the V2500.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: So Q3 was lifted a little bit by particularly strong content on the V program.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: So a little bit of growth there as well.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We see that actually slowing down in the fourth quarter, just on the mix of the inductions and the engines going through the shop.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: But as I said in the last call, we expected about 800 shop visits for 2026.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We are right on track to that rate through the end of the third quarter.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And we see no change to that outlook in the fourth quarter.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And frankly, I think we see that number of shop visit inductions pretty flat and consistent year over year with, again, increasing content on the V.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: But as we look at where we are today and the top line growth at Pratt, a lot of that's being driven off of our GTF program, which over time will far outweigh the structure decline in the V2500 powered aircraft.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: Thank you.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Thank you.

sentences.speaker: Operator
sentences.text: Thank you.

sentences.speaker: Operator
sentences.text: With that, I will now turn the call back over to Nathan Ware.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: All right.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Thank you, Lateef.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: That concludes today's call.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: As always, the investor relations team will be available for follow-up questions.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Thank you all for joining us and have a good day.

sentences.text: This now concludes today's conference.

sentences.text: As we continue to extend our industry leading scale in fiber, we are becoming more effective in how we plan, build, install, and calibrate the pace of our network deployment.

sentences.speaker: Management

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: But that's not inconsistent with the set of expectations that we've been building in this company and that we've used to drive our guidance to you over the long haul.

sentences.speaker: Management

sentences.speaker: Management

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And Dave, you are correct in saying that the level of promotions remains the same.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And the customer ultimately is going to bear the cost of higher device prices.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: With that said, there is a timing element.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: So generally, we pay for the devices within a relatively short term.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: So think about phones, tablets.

sentences.speaker: Management

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We pay upfront and we collect over time.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Typically the life of the customer.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Therefore, we are investing upfront and recovering it over time.

sentences.speaker: Management

sentences.speaker: Operator
sentences.text: The next question comes from Sean Diffley with Morgan Stanley.

sentences.speaker: Operator
sentences.text: Please go ahead.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: Great, thanks very much team.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: And congrats to Pascal on an awesome career.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: Two, if I may.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: The first on agentic and the second on CapEx and free cash flow outlook.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: So John, just an overarching question on how you're thinking about the potential rise of AI agents like Muse impacting the connectivity sector or not.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: You know, do you see this as a deflationary?

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: Do you see this as a deflationary force in the industry and a catalyst for switching and then talk about the risk and opportunity that you see for AT&T specifically?

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: And then on CapEx, I think it came down by about a billion for 27 and 28.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: You kept the free cash flow guide the same.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: I think you talked about improved efficiency on some of the fiber builds.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: I think the Mexico sale might be in there.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: But anything else we should be thinking about on the CapEx and free cash flow swings?

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: So, look, I think there's a lot that's happening.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: I think there's a lot that still is unpacked on, you know, what is technology in general, agentic search, agents, et cetera, going to do to everybody's funnel management?

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Pretend to know exactly how that's going to play out.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: I will tell you we're spending a lot of effort.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: There's many things we've been doing over the last several months and quarters to fine tune our strategies on how we make sure we stay relevant.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: I would tell you as different as it's going to be.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: I think it's going to be a lot of work.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: As different as it's going to be, what I'm encouraged by is we seem to be doing just fine and making the adjustments we need to make because there's been quite a bit of change already in how consumers are searching and looking for information and what they're doing around it.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And I think we're probably in the early innings of that.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: But we're aware of it.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We're adjusting to it.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: I think at the end of the day what's really important is you have good products.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And those good products have the right reputation and right value in the market.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And then ultimately you will be successful as you move forward.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And when you're operating in a position where you're putting technology out that's the lowest marginal cost technology that performs better, I think that puts us in a really good position to make sure we stay in that conversation moving forward.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Specifically to your question about MUSE and some of the other chatter that's going on right now, what I would tell you is philosophically we believe the customer gets to make choices.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: The customer gets to make choices on what they do with their service.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: That's always been our point of view.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: There's a need to dictate their path forward on things.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Customers have been pretty clear with us over the past number of years about account security, account management, account control.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Before agents ever showed up, there's all kinds of scenarios that go on today in real life that cause people to have to be really specific on who the decision-making authority is on their account.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We run family plans.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We have many, many people on them.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We have people whose life circumstances change where there's a responsible party and there's maybe a separation or marital discord that changes things.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: The notion of an account having an owner and a responsible party is not a new issue.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: As long as that responsible party is authorizing and making a transaction and can confirm that in the way that we would normally confirm those things, such as validating their identity and ensuring their authenticity, then we're going to be able to make decisions.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And that's what we're going to be doing.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Now, again, if everybody loves their identity and ensuring their authority, they should be able to do to their account whatever they want.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: If it's their agent that decides something needs to change and they've authorized an agent to do transactions on their account and we can authorize that transaction in the same way we would normally confirm, such as when there's a SIM swap or a major change on an account today.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We use things like two factor authentication to ensure that it's valid and confirm.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Those same principles and practices will be in place moving forward with agents.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: But the important thing is that the customer will control.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: They'll say whether or not their account is authorized to be managed by an agent.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And then if there is a large transaction that takes place, there will need to be a validation and authentication of that to ensure that we're not doing something that encourages fraud or is inconsistent with what the account owner would want to do.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: So all my point of view, just like today, is we want to make sure the customers feel like they're getting value for what they're buying.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We want to make sure they're right size to what they need in their products and services.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We do that as a normal course of business when people come into our stores and talk about what their needs are when they're working with us online and our algorithmic approach.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And the reality is that's very hard to do.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And in some cases there's been maybe more concentrated builds with the business model on legacy services and other things hasn't been aggressively managed to come up with an overall profitable equation.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And so we see the same thing.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: I think I'd answer it the same way I've answered it in the past.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Tell me the price and I'll give you the answer to the question.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And I think you've seen up to this point in time.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: I've been willing to go and acquire footprint and do things when I feel like we're getting.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And we think if the infrastructure has been built in a way that's consistent with our standards and our practices that we can operate it effectively over the long haul and the price is right.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Sure.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: I'd be interested in picking up more footprint if it holds to my point of view of us getting scale in the right geography.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: I don't want to just buy footprint for the sake of buying it.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: I need to make sure it bridges to.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Other parts of our network where we can have the kind of efficiencies and scale and advertising and the growth in our wireless business and all the things that we think kind of are the magic and the economics around that.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Lumen clearly fit that bill across the footprint that we picked up in my point of view.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: If other opportunities were like that that were priced that way.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Sure. I'd look at them as options and possibilities for us.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Right now I would say.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: In some cases, maybe.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Maybe there's expectations in that market that aren't consistent with what I just articulated.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Thanks for the question, Craig.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Operator, I think we have time for one more question.

sentences.speaker: Operator
sentences.text: The next question comes from Sam McHugh with BNP.

sentences.speaker: Operator
sentences.text: Please go ahead.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: Good morning, guys, and congrats, Pascal, as well.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: And welcome, Jennifer.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: On the fiber ARPUs, helpful color on the fourth quarter.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: With 27 guidance, do you anticipate a similar decline in fiber ARPUs as we're seeing at the moment?

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: And then secondly, on the whole.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: So fiber ARPUs, how do you see the future?

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: I think you raised this maybe a year or so ago first.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: Obviously, you lose a bit of kind of wholesale or cross-sell potential and wireless if you wholesale.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: Would you look for reciprocal fiber access from others as a precondition of wholesaling fiber?

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Thanks.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: The way to think about Q4 is, as I said, I expect Q4 to be down year over year around the same rate as we saw in Q3.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And I think that's a good thing.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: I think that's a good thing.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: That would imply a sequential moderation.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Overall, the guidance that we've given, if you recall, over the three-year period, is to have most of the growth.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: The vast majority of our growth is going to be driven by customer additions and not ARPU, not pricing.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And that continues to be our expectation.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: So, overall, we continue to expect relatively stable ARPU over this period.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Sam, on your…

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Sam, on your question about wholesale, your question infers you're thinking about it the right way, which is wholesale doesn't mean you have to open it up to all comers.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Wholesale could mean that you wholesale it to those that are more strategically positioned to help you in aggregate.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And an example of that, potentially there's a wholesaler who wants an exclusive MD&O relationship with you.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Or maybe there's a paired footprint somewhere else outside of existing fiber footprint that we have that we gain access to that we wouldn't have otherwise.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And also to your point, and as I indicated in my comments, you do this after you think you've run all the plays that are your highest value plays at retail.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: So our goal is to do everything we can to pick up every high value customer we can to serve at retail.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And we're having great success doing that.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: As you're seeing with the results that we've been sharing with you.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And we'll continue to run that play until we hit a place where we think we've topped out.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And I think what's important to understand is you don't have to make these decisions on a national basis.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: These can be very geographically driven.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And I think as over time, what we know, and I think what the cable industry would show you is a lot of these decisions and a lot of your approaches to market are local.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And they have to be.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: You look at what we've recently done in reorganizing our business.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: I don't know how many of you picked up on it.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We did a structural change in our consumer space in our go-to-market structure.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: The whole reason we did it is a realization that we're at a place where not all markets are created equal.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: There are differences in infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: There are differences in tactics that need to be used in particular geographies of the country.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Depending on what your asset base and the tactics you want to move forward.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And we needed to organize our business, our management teams.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And our incentives in a way that drove that.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And I think you're going to make those kind of decisions on a location by location and circumstance by circumstance basis.

sentences.speaker: Management
