sentences.speaker: Operator
sentences.text: Your line is open.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: Good morning.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: Good morning.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: I guess maybe this is the first question.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: The slide six where you have the national footprint.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: Just talk to us in terms of what the strategy around the client centers is.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: Obviously, you've seen many of your peers announce significant branch expansion in new markets.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: Is this a precursor to adding a ton of branches?

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: Or is this an indication that you don't see a ton of value adding hundreds of branches and the client centers allows you to achieve and reach the same outcomes?

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: I would love just your strategic sort of thought process behind that.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Good morning, Ibrahim.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: So I'll just start by saying we do see value in branches, and we do see them as anchoring very high-quality customer relationships.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Just to back up a little bit, we had been on a job, and we have been on a journey for really a decade to transform our branch network from what used to be a lot of small tier three service outlets to more advice hubs with most of our products being represented there.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: That was a renovation strategy that is finishing up now.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And we are beginning to lean into new branches.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We have shared that our branch investment has,

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: increased from 200 million or thereabouts on average to 300 million, which is what we expect to do going forward.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And those will be more new branches.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Our first phase of that work is to densify within our own footprint.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: As you see from the blue dots, we are in a vast territory.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And we have real meaningful opportunity to get to 8% to 10% growth.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: So we're going to be doing that.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We're going to be looking at a large portion of our brand share in those markets within our footprint that have high household formation rates.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: There our brand is already known, we are, our operations are already established,

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: and the return is very high.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: It is fully our expectation that over time, we will inch out from that footprint to other branches.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: The client centers on the other hand, are an interim answer, that is faster for us, national presence. This is not a new strategy. Our commercial teams, our wealth teams, our mortgage teams and our commercial real estate teams have been operating out of a footprint.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: The Northeast is a big site for capital markets type of businesses as well. And what we have done more recently is to say small business can also operate out of client centers. So

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: This call is being recorded and a webcast will be available for replay on our IR website. I would now like to turn the call over to Neeraj.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Thanks, Ryan, and good morning, everyone. We're pleased to be here to discuss our

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: third quarter results. Q3 was our strongest quarter of growth in the post-pandemic period, with total net revenue up 9.7% year over year and our U.S.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: business growing over 11%. That growth flowed through nicely to the bottom line with an adjusted EBITDA margin of 6.9%, our best Q3 results since 2020.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: At the start of this year, we told you we expected to take share in the U.S.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: at a pace we had not seen in several years. We entered 2025 with the U.S.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: share spread in the mid-single digits, widened it to high single digits by year end, and promised to push it into the double digits in 2026.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: With U.S. revenue growing double digits against a roughly flat category here in Q3,

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: we've done exactly that. That growth was driven by orders, which are up 12% year over year. That translated to strength in customer growth with active customers up more than 4% and new customer orders up over 14%, another post-pandemic record. The momentum we have on orders and customers gives us confidence that our share gains are structural because order growth compounds over time while AOV growth does not. We're very excited by the trajectory we're on and we're still in the early innings.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Earlier this year, I described the many pistons powering our engine of growth, and you're seeing their success in real time as they work in tandem. We're frequently asked which of these

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: initiatives is the strongest link to our share success. The answer is that it isn't any single one.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Programs like Wayfair Rewards, Wayfair Verified, Delivery Plus, our stores, along with long-standing businesses like Para Gold, our specialty retail brands, and Wayfair Professional all sit on top of a core recipe of assortment, availability, speed, and price that is the strongest it has been in our history.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Our core recipes are still early in their maturity and they compound on that core and on one another to produce outcomes like we just delivered in the third quarter.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Let me give you an example of how that works in practice. A shopper walks into one of our stores and discovers the depth of our catalog, including categories like bedding and tabletop she may never

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: have thought to buy from Wayfair. She joins Wayfair Rewards at checkout, giving her one more chance to buy a product. Her kitchen table arrives in days rather than weeks because we're sick close to our Castlegate fulfillment centers. And the next time she shops online, the verified badge helps her choose with confidence. She comes back more often, she benefits from low prices due to rewards, and for Wayfair, our ad costs have fallen, improving her customer lifetime value. And as she helps our volume grow, suppliers invest more in our platform and sharpen their pricing, which makes the offer even better for the next customer.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: That's why we have real confidence that our U.S. share spread can keep building into 2027 and beyond.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: You've heard us say this many times, but our success has been independent of the macro.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And when the category does return to growth, that spread will apply to a much larger base.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We're also following the same playbook now in our international markets, albeit at an earlier stage with more to roll out in the coming quarters. Our approach remains the same.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Grow faster than the market, flow that growth through to maximize adjusted EBITDA dollars, and keep reinvesting in what earns the customer's loyalty. The concept of loyalty is a critical one to our flywheel. We began this year talking about loyalty in the scope of our rewards program, and I now want to round out the year returning to the topic of loyalty and how we think about it across our marketing investments. Over the past two years, we've grown orders faster while spending less on advertising as a share of revenue, which was under

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: 10% this quarter for the first time since 2021. This is even as we've invested more in our brand and channels that are newer to the mix. So today I'd like to spend some time on what has driven that progress, why we believe it lasts, and where we're headed.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: The first driver is that more customers are coming to us directly. Rewards verified our stores and a better, faster site and app all give customers more reasons to start their shopping with Wayfair. In the third quarter, revenue from direct visits was up more than 15% from a year earlier. That comes in tandem with nice improvements in our core channels. For example, we've grown our text message audience by more than

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: 40% over the past year, with revenue from those texts up by more than 30%.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: The second driver is measurement, which has always been central to how we run Wayfair. From our earliest days, we've built our own in-house tools to understand what every marketing dollar returns, and that discipline is a big part of how we've stayed efficient.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Over the last few years, several things shifted at once. Privacy changes across the major platforms made traditional attribution less reliable, and customer behavior evolved in the post-pandemic environment, changing where and how people shop for their homes.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: In response to this, we've significantly increased how often we test, leaning more heavily on controlled experiments that isolate the true incremental impact of our spend.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Not surprisingly, that combination has surfaced opportunities to reallocate spend.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Where the spend was mostly reaching shoppers already on their way to Wayfair, we've pulled it back.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And where it reliably drives incremental sales, as with influencers, we're leaning in.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: The result is a roughly flat share count quarter over quarter.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: As we discussed, we intend to make this offset a recurring part of our capital allocation strategy while remaining opportunistic to modify when we believe it is appropriate.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Now let me turn to guidance for the fourth quarter. Starting with the top line, we would guide you to a high single-digit growth range for Q4.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We're pleased at the momentum we've seen to start the quarter, with Weyday last week nicely setting up the holiday events later this month.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Turning to gross margin, I would continue to guide you to the range of 29.5% to 30.5% of net revenue, once more targeting the lower portion of the range.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Customer service and merchant fees should be in line with what we delivered in Q3 as a percent of net revenue, and advertising should be in a 10.5% to 11.5% of net revenue range.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We do expect advertising as a percentage of revenue to come up in Q4 compared to Q3.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: As I mentioned a moment earlier, there is some seasonality at play as we lean in heavier during the holiday season, but would still expect healthy year-over-year leverage on advertising versus what we reported in the fourth quarter of 2025.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: SOTG&A should continue to be in a range of $360-370 million. Working your way down the P&L, we would expect adjusted EBITDA margin in a range of 6% to 7% of net revenue for the fourth quarter.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Now let me touch on a few housekeeping items. We expect equity-based compensation and related taxes of roughly $60-70 million. Depreciation and amortization should be approximately $59 million to $65 million.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Net interest expense of approximately $42 million. Weighted average shares outstanding of approximately $138 million.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: CAPEX in a $70 million to $80 million range. You're beginning to see this line item grow as we ramp up our investment in stores, and that will continue into 2027.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Of course, this is all in the construct of strong performance from our stores, which allows us to self-fund that growth while still driving robust and growing free cash flow.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: As we head into the holiday season and look ahead to 2027, I want to step back for a moment.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: A year ago, we told you we would invest judiciously to grow the business at a rapid pace while growing adjusted EBITDA faster than revenue, and that is exactly what this quarter shows.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Our US share spread is now in the double digits. That growth is coming from orders and customers. We are spending less to acquire each of these customers, and more of each incremental dollar is reaching the bottom line.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: In adjusted EBITDA, in net income, and in free cash flow. With a stronger balance sheet and a share account we are tightly controlling, we are turning that growth into more value per share.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Most of the initiatives Neeraj described are still early, and we believe the best of this compounding is still ahead of us.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Thank you, and with that, Neeraj, Steve, and I will take your questions.

sentences.speaker: Operator
sentences.text: We will now begin the question and answer session. Please limit yourself to one question and one follow-up.

sentences.speaker: Operator
sentences.text: If you would like to ask a question, please press star one to raise your hand. To withdraw your question, press star one again.

sentences.speaker: Operator
sentences.text: We ask that you pick up your handset when asking a question to allow for optimum sound quality. If you are muted locally, please remember to unmute your device.

sentences.speaker: Operator
sentences.text: Please stand by while we compile the Q&A roster. Your first question comes from the line of Simeon Gutman with Morgan Stanley. Your line is open. Please go ahead.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: Good morning, everyone. Thanks for taking our question. So my first question is on loyalty.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: Can you talk about how pleased you are with the level of growth you are getting and the level of, call it gross profit, dollar growth?

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: And Neeraj, is there a way to tell us the level of inning that you are with this? Does this completely change your ability to talk to consumers?

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: It feels like it is only a couple of quarters in. And I want to ask how much, I guess the share spread, are we early in the share spread equation?

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: Could that even grow even further? Thanks.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Thanks for your question. Yeah, let me start with loyalty. So on loyalty, I'd say we're very pleased. We launched it not quite, probably about two years ago.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And what we've seen is it's been growing at a nice rate. But to your question about innings and the growth ahead of us, the way to think about it is there's a lot that's ahead of us because you get sort of the folks who are paying the most attention, your most interested customers early.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: But a lot of what we think is ahead of us is the program has very substantial benefits. And when we talk to customers about it, they get very excited about it.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: It would still be relatively easy for a customer to be unaware of the program. And so if you think about all the places on our services where we can help existing members know of all the benefits, additional benefits they have so we get more dollars per year from them and gross profit dollars per year as you ask.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Or when you think about the much larger number of people who have not yet joined, where they can then learn about what the program is, the benefits they get, and then sign up.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And then once they sign up, the behavior changes because they want to take advantage of the program that they just joined. That's still ahead of us.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: So I would say that we think we're, in terms of innings, it's not the first inning, but it's not far into the game, call it the third inning or something, second inning.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: It's pretty early in the game. And we think this can ramp to be a much higher percentage of revenue than it is today.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And as you know, the core tenet of the program is that it offers the customers really tangible value in a way that encourages them to consider us much more top of mind as their go-to place for all things home, getting them buying across more categories.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And so if you're doing both equally well, the 80 would hold. Ultimately, if you get bigger and bigger, you might say there's less new customers to get. And so the repeat could grow.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: I think at the end of the day, the repeat number should be pretty high because if repeat's not working, then the business is not working in retail. If you're not delivering your customers a good experience, they're not coming back.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Whether you have a problem in the near term or the midterm, you're going to have a problem. And so we tend to look at repeat on a narrower definition, which is our net repeat rate.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: So different customer cohorts, how often are they coming back? And so it's not the metrics that are easy to see when you zoom out to the total because that has a lot mixed into it together.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: But basically, we're seeing repeat strengthening and climbing, whether that's a more loyal customer or that's a relatively new customer to the brand, whether that's an e-com only customer, that's a customer, e-com customer who's then experienced stores and then what they do.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: So we cut it up many, many ways. And so we're seeing that all going the right way, which is effectively the leading indicator of your future revenue and your future revenue growth rate.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: In terms of how the guidance, the piano is shaped, let me turn it over to you.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Chris, I'm impressed that you can pull a model from 12 years ago that I'm embarrassed to say I was probably involved in developing. So thank you for the callback.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: But as it speaks to sort of AC&R leverage, clearly we are seeing some nice momentum on AC&R leverage over the past 12 months.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And I think a number of the things that Neeraj mentioned are helping to drive that. So loyalty is something that should drive AC&R leverage and structural improvement over time.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Further order, volume growth and repeat growth, to your point, does drive AC&R leverage. And you see that start to show up and repeat order growth has actually grown quite nicely over the last several quarters.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Neeraj shared a stat on his call when he was talking about the marketing spend saying that revenue associated with direct traffic is up 15% year over year.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: So you're seeing that momentum and that push that does help give more structural AC&R leverage.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: That said, we do see some seasonality here. So I just want to remind folks that we sort of called out some of the improvements this quarter, maybe hit a little bit better because of the seasonality that we might see in the fourth quarter.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And, you know, we noted that obviously in the guide, but over time you have seen that nice engagement there.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Thanks so much.

sentences.speaker: Operator
sentences.text: Your next question comes from the line of Oliver Wintermantel with Evercore ISI. Your line is open. Please go ahead.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: Thanks. Good morning, guys. So your contribution margin reached 16.1% despite lower gross margins.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: And as we think about full Q&A next year, how much of that improvement is sustainable and where do you think you have to reinvest?

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Yeah, Kate, why don't you?

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: I'll start. So the first thing I point to is, you know, we've talked for some quarters now about 15% being sort of a general place where we're operating contribution margin from.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Is that the right position to, as we talked about a few questions ago, really hit on that place of accelerating revenue growth and accelerating EBITDA dollar growth faster than that revenue growth?

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: So that 15% place seems to be generally, you know, sort of the right balance of trade-off on that gross margin and the AC&R.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Obviously this quarter you did see that accelerate a little bit.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Again, as we just talked about with Chris, some of that is due to the seasonality of the marketing spend.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And so in the guide, you know that that goes back to roughly that 15% place for next quarter.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: I think the thing, just to zoom back out, right, we were talking a few minutes ago about EBITDA dollar growth and margin rate and what we're trying to do.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: So think about the business. Ultimately, what we'd like to have is a very large business.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: So that was that that's revenue with a very large amount of profit.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Right. And what is that? That's that's that's EBITDA dollars or the owner's earnings, EBITDA less cash flow, whatever way you want to think about.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: But ultimately it's what's the true intrinsic profit associated with that revenue.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Right. And so then the question is like, how do you get there? So the strategy of how we get there is what we talked about.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Right. We believe in the recipe. We believe in programs. We believe in product led growth.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We think these things are really going to do that strategy executed well.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We'll get this outcome. So then when you start going to like lines in between on the P&L, those lines have a number of things and trades in them.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: But ultimately, the way you can tell if you're making the right trades is going to be the combination of, you know, what is what is that revenue growth and the revenue dollars and where the profit dollars.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And if you're growing the profits faster than you're growing the revenue, your margin rate will continue to tick up.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And at that point, our view is what you'd want to do is not worry about the margin rate speed of going up.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Like the, you know, basically the velocity. What you want to worry about is are you maximizing the dollars as you go?

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Because ultimately you want to get to the biggest dollars and the margin rate will keep climbing if you do exactly what I said.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Well, but if you optimize for the margin rate, you may end up with less dollars than you could otherwise.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Right. So you want to do both, which is you're growing the margin rate, but that's secondary to growing the dollars.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And so you're growing the margin rate while growing the dollars, the maximal amount.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And you're doing that by balancing the margin rate contribution with the profit with the revenue contribution times the margin rate.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Right. And so the lines in between, you know, to our mind, there's always tradeoffs and we're going to optimize those to get the outcome I just described.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: Got it. Thank you. And then just on internationally, the last widened to 25 million.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: So can you maybe talk about what is driving the deterioration there and what needs to change before the US growth initiatives can translate into better international results?

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: I'm sorry, just a second. But let me just say, you know, I tried to address this in the script.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: I think the thing to realize is like when we when we talked about how we got our tech cycles back, we're able to focus on programs and focus on product led growth.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: There's a little bit of a sequence to that. And we prioritize wayfair.com as the first place we did that work.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: So you can see that by like some elements like when did we launch rewards?

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: They come more direct. They're more engaged. They buy across categories, actually, as you just mentioned in the first question.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And so they have sort of a broader base experience with us. And we think that's going quite well.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: So we would say that that was an intentional strategy to sort of overall drive the flywheel that drives that EBITDA dollar growth, but then does, yes, have some impact on the gross margin.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: But the net of all of that is that contribution margin sort of 15 percent ish.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: Very helpful. I hope you guys have a great holiday. Thank you so much.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Thank you. You too, Michael.

sentences.speaker: Operator
sentences.text: Your next question comes from the line of Peter Keith with Piper Sandler. Your line is open. Please go ahead.

sentences.speaker: Operator
sentences.text: Thank you. Good morning. Nice quarter, guys.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: You know, Kate, you just mentioned the last comment around loyalty, making your business more efficient, more profitable.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: Something you could update us on where you guys stand from a loyalty membership count.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: I think you came into the year with a little over a million, maybe a goal of doubling it.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: How has that been going?

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: Do you think you're on track to at least double it in 2026?

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: Yeah, we do from time to time give updates on programs like loyalty.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We're feeling good about the momentum and, you know, overall sort of engagement there.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: I think there's two pieces that that we're focused on there.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: One is the members, as you mentioned, we feel like we're on track.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: That's going well. The second is the engagement of those members.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: So getting them to sort of increase that incrementality of spend and, you know, that's going well. It's going well as well.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: All right. Well, we'll put it over to to stores.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: You know, it's maybe a little early, but you do have the Atlanta and Columbus stores now open.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: Are those seeing a similar type of performance as the Chicago store in its early months?

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: And then related to that, I'm wondering if if some of this like the store success begets more success.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: In other words, our landlords start to realize that that you guys are driving traffic or can become a large tenant.

sentences.speaker: Analyst
sentences.text: Are you starting to get more calls and better real estate deals as you're looking to expand that real estate pipeline?

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Yeah, thanks. I'll make a couple of comments and then also Kate can join in and add any thoughts she has.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: So landlords are seeing that our stores draw significant traffic that we've seen them be very keen to get us into their centers.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: We've continued to stay very disciplined and picky about which centers we think fit what we want.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And we're also learn continue to learn a lot about the right size space, the right type of space, the right trade area, the right location in the trade area, like right co-tenancy.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And because the landlords are pretty keen to get us, we're able to combine sort of getting what we need and the right economics to get the financial outcomes we want.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: So that's been pretty that's been a pretty clear signal.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: As we have more stores open and they're replicable in terms of seeing those strong results.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: That's the other thing I think the landlords have noticed because they'll they'll visit multiple locations and they say, OK, oh, geez, I'm very strong view of what I'm going to get here.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: And they kind of there's not a lot of concepts that are growing that there can be draws like this.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: So, yeah, that's all going quite well.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: Yeah, Peter, to your specific question on how are Atlanta and Columbus performing?

sentences.speaker: Management

sentences.text: And so we've got really good confidence that we've got more ability to continue to do that and that'll be pretty stable.

sentences.speaker: Management
sentences.text: So that sort of underpins sort of the NIM being pretty stable as we go into Q4.

sentences.text: What's happening in Q4 then is you start to get the benefits of a lot of what you started seeing in Q3.

sentences.text: I think we were up the end of periods up 15 billion or so, going into the fourth quarter.

sentences.text: And so you're getting the benefit of that in the fourth quarter.

sentences.text: You know, we continue to grow deposits.

sentences.text: And then there are a few other factors that sort of drive it, but those are sort of the big ones that sort of, you know, lead to the step up that we're gonna see going into Q4.
